other_failure_modes.name: Data Leakage via Test Set Vocabulary
other_failure_modes.description: The categorical encoding vocabulary is constructed by taking the union of unique values from both the training and test sets. This leaks knowledge of the test data distribution into the training pipeline, which violates strict test-set isolation.

other_failure_modes.name: Improper Submission ID Generation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent fails to extract and preserve the actual identifier column from the test dataset for the submission file. Instead, it generates a sequential range of IDs, which will cause the submission to be misaligned or invalid if the test dataset uses specific non-sequential IDs.

summary: The agent implements a generally solid 5-fold cross-validation pipeline utilizing three gradient boosting frameworks (LightGBM, CatBoost, XGBoost) and performs reasonable data cleaning and datetime extraction. However, the final ensemble relies on naive, hardcoded weights rather than tuning them using validation predictions. Additionally, there are critical flaws in how the agent constructs the categorical vocabulary (leaking test data information) and how it generates the submission file IDs (hallucinating sequential numbers rather than using actual test IDs).
